_doc: W316 — DECLARED EXCEPTIONS TO THE TENANT SCOPE FENCE.
An entry here is INERT ON ITS OWN. The fence requires BOTH this entry AND a
'/* TENANT-SCOPE-EXEMPT: <key> */' marker immediately above the statement it
excuses. A marker with no entry FAILS the build ('an undeclared exception'),
and an entry with no marker FAILS the build as STALE ('an exception that
outlived the code it excused'). Two places, both required, both checked in
both directions — because a one-place exception list is how a fence quietly
'ruling' must name the authority that decided the read may cross tenants.
'countervailingControl' must name what keeps the exception honest: an
exception with nothing standing against it is an unbounded permission.

exemptions.ruling: Slide13b delegated lead-developer decision, 2026-09-20: the approved invitation identity binding must detect all conflicting identities before tenant selection. This is a declared global identity read, not a sacred waiver or baseline change.
reason: A person may belong to multiple companies and partner teams. Restricting identity resolution to the invited company tenant would misclassify an existing account as new or conceal duplicate IDs.
countervailingControl: Email is taken from a hash-matched invitation, not an arbitrary public lookup. All matching durable IDs are compared; ambiguity, deletion and lookup errors fail closed. Ownership requires an exact HMAC-verified non-revoked session, live canonical user and account-status gate. Candidate identities and credential material are not returned.

exemptions.ruling: Slide13b delegated lead-developer decision, 2026-09-20: verify signup identity globally by exact generated ID and invitation email before ownership is granted.
reason: The canonical signup assigns a user-home tenant rather than the invited company tenant. A company-tenant condition would reject valid signup without adding identity protection.
countervailingControl: Exact generated user ID, normalized invitation email and non-deleted row are mandatory. Durable credential and strict cross-source identity agreement are separately verified inside the signup transaction. Failure rolls back partial identity writes before claim or session issuance.
exemptions.provenAfterChange: server/__tests__/slide13b_a0_team_identity_http.test.ts: new-user persistence and SQL-trigger rollback controls.

exemptions.ruling: Slide13b delegated lead-developer decision, 2026-09-20: rollback cleanup must check every canonical identity source for the exact newly returned ID before evicting its credential cache.
reason: Tenant filtering could hide a durable identity and make cleanup unsafe. The query is exact-ID existence protection, not a listing of other users.
countervailingControl: Runs only after failed fresh signup and never for alreadyExisted. Exact ID is checked across users, auth_users and credentials; any durable row prevents cleanup. It never deletes canonical identity rows.
exemptions.provenAfterChange: server/__tests__/slide13b_a0_team_identity_http.test.ts: failed persistence, credential-cache cleanup and runtime-ghost controls.

exemptions.ruling: Slide13b delegated lead-developer decision, 2026-09-20: revalidate the exact invited identity within the atomic claim, independently of its home tenant.
reason: Legitimate cross-company and partner/founder identities have a user-home tenant different from the company receiving the membership.
countervailingControl: Exact durable ID and invitation email plus non-deleted users row are required inside the final transaction. Strict identity resolution is repeated; matching signed session and account-status checks remain mandatory. No existing-account cookie or password is issued or changed.
exemptions.provenAfterChange: server/__tests__/slide13b_a0_team_identity_http.test.ts: claim-time identity changes, orphan identity refusal and cross-role positive controls.

exemptions.ruling: Owner ruling Q10 — the cohort benchmark MUST STAY CROSS-TENANT.
reason: A benchmark computed inside one tenant is not a benchmark. It compares a
GP's portfolio to itself and returns approximately 1.00 by construction,
which is worse than no number: it looks like a peer comparison and is not
one. The whole product value of this read is that the cohort spans the
platform.
No individual subject's figures are disclosed by it: the read returns one
aggregate, gated on 'benchmark.min_cohort_n' so a cohort small enough to
re-identify a member is refused outright.
countervailingControl: WAVE 221 (R190.10) — subjects who opt out of benchmarking are filtered
OUT WHERE THE NUMBER IS MADE, in this same function, not at display time.
shared/wave221BenchmarkingOptOutCopy.ts carries the user-facing copy and
server/__tests__/w221_benchmarking_opt_out.test.ts is the guard.
'benchmark.min_cohort_n' (wave9_reporting_config) is the k-anonymity floor.
exemptions.provenAfterChange: server/__tests__/w316_cross_tenant_reporting_scope.test.ts asserts this read STILL returns a cohort assembled from more than one tenant after W316.

exemptions.ruling: Owner question Q-D, delegated and decided in W316: DO NOT SCOPE THIS READ. W303 explicitly protected the '/api/me/**' surface.
reason: This read is IDENTITY-scoped, which is TIGHTER than tenant-scoped, not
looser: 'WHERE lp_id IN (resolveInvestorIdSet(canonicalUserId))' returns
only rows belonging to the caller themselves.
Adding a tenant predicate here would REMOVE ROWS THE LP LEGITIMATELY OWNS.
An LP who has committed to vehicles under two different GPs owns cashflows
under two tenant ids; scoping '/api/me/cashflows' to one of them would
silently drop half of their own distributions from their own DPI. That is
not a smaller leak — it is a WRONG NUMBER on the investor's own statement.
Re-verified in W316 by reading the SQL and censusing the call sites: one
production caller, server/lib/reportingEngineRoutes.ts, route
GET /api/me/cashflows. The exclusion in the specification HELD.
countervailingControl: 'resolveInvestorIdSet' (server/lib/investorIdentityAliasStore.ts) is the
single decider of which ids denote the caller, and an empty set returns [],
never an unfiltered read. The route sits behind the authenticated /api/me
surface, so lp_id is derived from the session and never from the request.
exemptions.provenAfterChange: server/__tests__/w316_cross_tenant_reporting_scope.test.ts drives GET /api/me/cashflows as a CONTROL and asserts it still returns the LP's own cross-tenant rows.

exemptions.ruling: Owner question Q-E, delegated and decided in W316: derive the tenant from the caller's own holdings.
reason: This is the read that DERIVES the tenant scope, so it cannot itself be
tenant-scoped — there is nothing to scope it to yet. Requiring a tenant
here would be circular.
It is instead scoped by the caller's own identity, with the SAME predicate
'investorHoldsCompany' already trusts to authorise the request:
investor_id = caller, company_id = the company in the path,
state = 'committed', deleted_at IS NULL. It reads no figure of any kind —
only the DISTINCT tenant ids of the caller's own committed holdings.
server/lib/userContext.ts, which would otherwise be the place to carry a
tenant id, is FROZEN this wave and carries none.
countervailingControl: Fails CLOSED: an unreadable table, a thrown query, or a blank tenant_id
yields an empty array, and GET /api/investor/portfolio/:id/marks turns an
empty scope into the same byte-identical 404 it already returns for 'you do
not hold this company'. It cannot widen a read.
asTenantScope() refuses an empty scope, so 'scope to nothing' — which would
return an empty chart to everyone and pass a naive leak test — is not
expressible.
exemptions.provenAfterChange: server/__tests__/w316_cross_tenant_reporting_scope.test.ts proves tenant A sees A's OWN marks first, then that A cannot see B's, over real HTTP.

exemptions.ruling: WAVE 344 ITEM 2, owner brief: 'Archived records REMAIN VISIBLE in audit and admin views. Hiding from a working view is not hiding from the record.'
reason: This is the audit and administrator view of archiving decisions. Its whole
purpose is that an archived record cannot vanish from the record, and an
audit view that can only see one tenant at a time cannot answer 'has
anything been archived' for the platform the owner is responsible for.
The function DOES accept an optional tenantId and applies it when given, so
a scoped read is available; the unscoped read is the deliberate audit case.
Nothing here is a customer record. The table holds ARCHIVING DECISIONS
ONLY: which kind of thing, which id, archived or restored, when, by whom,
and a free-text reason. It carries no name, no email, no note, no stage, no
money and no hash anchor, because it is a separate registry table and not a
column added to the records themselves.
countervailingControl: The route is gated requireAuth + requireAdmin, and its response is labelled
surface: 'archive-decisions-only' so an operator reading it is not left to
assume it is a record viewer.
Owner rulings R285/R289 — an administrator may read founder CONTACT DETAILS
but NOT founder CRM RECORDS. That boundary is enforced by the table shape
above and guarded by server/__tests__/w344_item3_admin_founder_crm_boundary.test.ts,
which archives a contact carrying a private marker note and FAILS if that
note, or the contact's name or email, appears anywhere in the admin
response. It also asserts the stored row has exactly 10 columns and that
every one of them is an archiving-decision field.
The single-row read in the same module (readRow) is tenant-scoped and takes
no exemption, so this entry covers the audit listing and nothing else.
